newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Daewoo says consortium finds oil off Angola.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo says consortium finds oil off Angola.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Corp said on Tuesday a multi-national consortium, led by Total SA of France, had found oil off Angola.
The oil field is estimated to have oil reserves equivalent of 6,400 barrels per day, Daewoo said in a statement.
Commercial production at the field is expected to start in late 1998 at the earliest, the statement said.
Total SA holds a 40 percent stake in the consortium, while South Korea's Daewoo Corp and Korea Petroleum Development Corp hold 18.75 percent and 6.25 percent stakes, respectively.
Two other partners in the consortium are Angola's state-run Sonangol with a 25 percent stake and South Africa's Engen Ltd with a 10 percent stake, it said.
Daewoo is a foreign trading and construction unit of Daewoo Group DWGR.CN, one of South Korea's top five conglomerates.
